summary: Read-only audit complete; lead remains INCOMPLETE, not already verified. PASS for explicit owner/World checks and persistence logic in supplied route source. UNVERIFIED for current runtime isolation, authenticated original 96-answer retention, restart durability and MP20 immediate Plan persistence. Existing reports describe synthetic integration successes, including sampled legacy continuity, but execution artifacts were not supplied. REWORK is needed to reconcile conflicting acceptance statements and close evidence gaps.
knownLimitations: Only supplied excerpts and code blocks were reviewed; no filesystem, Git status, commands, network calls or provider calls were used.
No actual test execution evidence was supplied; tests is intentionally empty.
Manifest hashes identify supplied evidence but were not independently recomputed.
Authentication helpers, database RLS/RPC definitions, full legacy routing/storage code, raw test outputs, screenshots and pre/post-restart snapshots were not supplied.
A reported genuine Gemini response elsewhere in the MP17 report was not saved to a Plan; fixture persistence does not prove persistence of live provider output.
Same-day report ordering is not sufficient to establish which build matches all current source.
blockers: Original authenticated 96-question answer preservation cannot be accepted without an authoritative persisted answer source or an explicit clarification of the legacy retention requirement.
Current-build runtime acceptance cannot be independently established from report narratives and test definitions alone.
nextSuggestedSteps: Provide an authenticated legacy-account regression artifact for an isolated synthetic existing account: compare baseline profile, World ID, Plan versions/goals and equipment before and after login, EN/VI switching and reload; assert no forced new onboarding or duplicate goals. Identify the authoritative original-answer source, or explicitly retain that dimension as unverified.

Exercise the current MP20 immediate Plan flow with Advisor intercepted before World entry: A/B/Custom save/readback, unrelated-goal preservation, uncheck, zero goals, reload, rejected writes and cross-account profile/Plan access. Supply build identity and sanitized assertion output.

For restart durability, capture owner/World/Plan/equipment identifiers before a controlled isolated restart and compare them afterward; do not rely solely on same-ID checks between two post-restart reads.
Reconcile the activation/inference contradictions and historical answer-retention claims in the affected acceptance reports using dated, build-specific evidence.
auditFindings: PASS — source authorization boundary: src/app/api/healthclues/profile/route.ts checks the authenticated user's ownership of the requested World before GET/PATCH, scopes profile access to auth.id, requires confirmed email for PATCH and merges preferences into existing profile JSON. The imported authentication/service helpers and database policies were not supplied; their behavior remains unverified.

PASS — source persistence contract: src/app/api/healthclues/plan/route.ts checks owner/World access on GET/POST, requires verified email and explicit confirmation for writes, supports empty goals, reuses matching request keys and appends versioned Plans to profile JSON while retaining at most 40 history records. Generated goals require signed proof or matching previously accepted content. This establishes implemented logic, not successful runtime persistence or concurrent-write safety.

PASS — source account scoping: src/app/api/healthclues/account/route.ts scopes deletion-status reads and deletion/cancellation RPC parameters to auth.id. RPC implementations and deletion lifecycle execution were not supplied, so purge/recovery behavior is UNVERIFIED.

PASS — existing automated test coverage is present: scripts/test-healthclues-profile-activity-rest-e2e.mjs defines direct local PostgREST/database integration assertions for consented profile save/revision/history/delete, activity persistence, anonymous denial and cross-user reads. It creates synthetic database users and signs JWTs locally; it does not exercise real email authentication, Next routes, World/Plan continuity or original 96-answer retention. Its success log is code, not execution evidence.
